name: CF1: chemical-unit collective feedback
status: 2026-10-08 14:28 CST: collective seed71 completed4096 actual CUDA updates. Its generation is scheduled onGPU4 after the existing dense-query71 pipeline exits. Control71, collective72 and control72 are now training concurrently. No CF1 generated-quality panel or efficacy result yet.
question: Does intra-denoising-step communication between chemical units improve joint atomic geometry and collective motion beyond equal-budget continuation of the internal-time baseline?

arms.control: Same-seed final placement model +4096 updates; no collective module
arms.collective: Same parent +4096 updates; add globally communicating pooled chemical-unit features before final two geometry layers

architecture: Existing observed-history and joint-query temporal attention (dynamic only)
Pool scalars/vectors by sample+component+block; global invariant-weight/equivariant-vector attention; gated lift to atoms (static and dynamic)
Original atom geometry layers 7–8, output normalization and velocity/drift heads
no_changes: query selection or data schedule between arms
fairness: Same-seed warmstart; fresh optimizer in both arms, not exact resume
Same data/task/query schedule and same dedicated source/bridge-noise generator
New collective parameters and FLOPs are the intervention; not equal-parameter or equal-compute comparison
Extra module initialization consumes global torch RNG but no dropout is introduced; dedicated bridge generator remains seeded identically
Existing placement versus interleaved comparison is not this experiment's matched control
static_policy: 25% static updates through the same collective+atom geometry path; temporal attention bypasses singleton static examples; corrupted positions only

evaluation.protein: 48 fixed development systems, 2 observed anchors, 2 draws; native100 and80ps
evaluation.complex: 64 fixed systems, old16/new48 reported separately; 2 anchors and8 draws; native80ps
criteria: Bond/angle/torsion/clashes together with MSD/RMSF and complete-path energy scores
Ligand collective translation/pocket/contact distribution together with internal bond fluctuation
Protein temporal order relative to MD, not maximizing smoothness
Both training seeds; no best-checkpoint/sample selection
Predictive-distribution comparisons use fair joint-pair path ES with S*(S-1); retain empirical S^2 results only for traceability. Existing main whole-path scores already use the fair estimator
evaluation.references: Untouched released PVB; BioKinema native1ns follow-up only if joint geometry/motion remains promising
limitations: Development evidence, not held-out family/scaffold generalization
Short trajectories do not prove equilibrium or kinetic rates
One block-feedback insertion does not guarantee learned long-range dynamics

This isolated placement-parent fork uses attention-only time conditioning, not the separate direct-lag FiLM branch; it does not repair the known H1/Q1 clock degeneracy. A successful collective module must still be evaluated together with direct physical-time conditioning before general-model promotion
Pooling may erase multimodal intrablock motion; atom stream and local geometry remain intact
No explicit component-wide rigid-body or shared stochastic mode is implemented in CF1

next_mechanisms_not_implemented: Repeat temporal/coarse-spatial/local-spatial interaction through multiple trunk stages if CF1 learns useful communication
Joint collective translation/rotation and internal residual readout, without freezing internal deformations
Structured spatiotemporal stochastic source only with mathematically consistent interpolation target and sampler; do not merely correlate inference noise
Physical-time Mamba may operate on interacting chemical-unit states; replacing atomwise temporal modules alone does not create spatial cooperation

sources.use: ATMOS atom-to-token encoder, single/pair recurrent state and geometry decoder; conceptual precedent, not a reproduced model
Released dynamics model with spatial modeling and physical-time temporal attention; untouched reference
